31555-under-the-liberty-tree-a-story-of-.title: American History,
31555-under-the-liberty-tree-a-story-of-.creator: James Otis.
31555-under-the-liberty-tree-a-story-of-.description: A book by James Otis.. "Your Lordship must know that Liberty Tree is a large, old Elm in  the High Street, upon which the effigies were hung in the time of  the Stamp Act, and from whence the mobs at that time made their  parades. It has since been adorned with an inscription, and has  obtained the name of Liberty Tree, as the ground under it has  that of Liberty Hall.

573-tales-from-shakespeare.title: Tales From Shakespeare
573-tales-from-shakespeare.creator: Charles And Mary Lamb
573-tales-from-shakespeare.description: A book by Charles And Mary Lamb. It has been wished to make these Tales easy reading for very young children. To the utmost of their ability the writers have constantly kept this in mind; but the subjects of most of them made this a very difficult task. It was no easy matter to give the histories of men and women in terms familiar to the apprehension of a very young mind.

arxiv-2106-15785.title: Dynamic Imaging using Deep Bi-linear Unsupervised Regularization (DEBLUR)
arxiv-2106-15785.creator: Abdul Haseeb Ahmed, Prashant Nagpal, and Mathews Jacob
arxiv-2106-15785.description: Abstract Bilinear models that decompose dynamic data to spatial and temporal factors are powerful and memory-efficient tools for the recovery of dynamic MRI data. These methods rely on sparsity and energy compaction priors on the factors to regularize the recovery. The quality of the recovered images depend on the specific priors.

arxiv-2204-08548.title: State-Output Risk-Constrained Quadratic Control of Partially Observed Linear Systems
arxiv-2204-08548.creator: Nikolas Koumpis, Anastasios Tsiamis, Dionysios Kalogerias
arxiv-2204-08548.description: Abstract We propose a methodology for performing risk-averse quadratic regulation of partially observed Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems, disturbed by process and output noise. To compensate against the induced variability due to both types of noises, state regulation is subject to two risk constraints.

arxiv-2310-19579.title: A Navigation Logic for Recursive Programs with Dynamic Thread Creation
arxiv-2310-19579.creator: Roman Lakenbrink, Markus Müller-Olm, Christoph Ohrem, Jens Gutsfeld
arxiv-2310-19579.description: Abstract Dynamic Pushdown Networks (DPNs) are a model for multithreaded programs with recursion and dynamic creation of threads. In this paper, we propose a temporal logic called NTL for reasoning about the call- and return- as well as thread creation behaviour of DPNs.

arxiv-2401-04789.title: On combinatorial properties of Gruenberg–Kegel graphs of finite groups
arxiv-2401-04789.creator: Mingzhu Chen, Ilya Gorshkov, Natalia V. Maslova, Nanying Yang
arxiv-2401-04789.description: Abstract If G G is a finite group, then the spectrum ω ⁡ ( G ) \omega(G) is the set of all element orders of G G . The prime spectrum π ⁡ ( G ) \pi(G) is the set of all primes belonging to ω ⁡ ( G ) \omega(G) .

arxiv-2507-14912.title: Redefining Elderly Care with Agentic AI: Challenges and Opportunities
arxiv-2507-14912.creator: Ruhul Amin Khalil, Kashif Ahmad, Hazrat Ali
arxiv-2507-14912.description: Abstract The global ageing population necessitates new and emerging strategies for caring for older adults. In this article, we explore the potential for transformation in elderly care through Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI), powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). We discuss the proactive and autonomous decision-making facilitated by Agentic AI in elderly care.

arxiv-2511-03953.title: Conditional Score Learning for Quickest Change Detection in Markov Transition Kernels
arxiv-2511-03953.creator: Wuxia Chen, Taposh Banerjee, Vahid Tarokh
arxiv-2511-03953.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wuxia Chen, Taposh Banerjee, Vahid Tarokh. We address the problem of quickest change detection in Markov processes with unknown transition kernels. The key idea is to learn the conditional score ∇ 𝐲 ​ log ​ p ​ ( 𝐲 | 𝐱 ) \nabla_{\mathbf{y}}\log p(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}) directly from sample pairs ( 𝐱 , 𝐲 ) (\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) , where both 𝐱 \mathbf{x} and 𝐲 \mathbf{y} are high-dimensional data generated by the same transition kernel.

arxiv-2511-17093.title: The Two-Measure Theory and an Overview of Some of its Manifestations
arxiv-2511-17093.creator: A. B. Kaganovich
arxiv-2511-17093.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A. B. Kaganovich. The Two-Measure theory (TMT) has been developing since 1998 and has yielded a number of highly interesting results, including those not realized in traditional field theory models. The most important advantage of TMT as an alternative theory is that, under the conditions under which all classical tests of general relativity are performed, TMT models are able to accurately reproduce Einstein’s general relativity. Despite this, TMT is still often perceived as something too exotic to be relevant to reality.

arxiv-2601-22440.creator: Bhada Yun, Renn Su, April Yi Wang
arxiv-2601-22440.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Bhada Yun, Renn Su, April Yi Wang. Does AI understand human values? While this remains an open philosophical question, we take a pragmatic stance by introducing VAPT, the Value-Alignment Perception Toolkit, for studying how LLMs reflect people’s values and how people judge those reflections. 20 participants texted a chatbot over a month, then completed a 2-hour interview with our toolkit evaluating AI’s ability to extract (pull details regarding), embody (make decisions guided by), and explain (provide proof of) their values.

britannica-1911-contat-louise-francoise.title: Contat, Louise Françoise (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-contat-louise-francoise.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-contat-louise-francoise.description: Article 'Contat, Louise Françoise' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 7), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. CONTARINI, the name of a distinguished Venetian family, who gave to the republic eight doges and many other eminent citizens. The story of their descent from the Roman family of Cotta, appointed prefects of the Reno valley (whence Cotta Reni or Conti del Reno), is probably a legend. One Mario Contarini was among the twelve electors of the doge Paulo Lucio Anafesto in 697.

plos-pone-0004937.creator: Tingqing Guo, William Jou, Tatyana Chanturiya et al.
plos-pone-0004937.description: PLOS ONE research article. Myostatin (Mstn) is a secreted growth factor expressed in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue that negatively regulates skeletal muscle mass. Mstn −/− mice have a dramatic increase in muscle mass, reduction in fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced and genetic obesity. To determ

pmc-10650556.title: Revolutionizing Urban Mobility: IoT-Enhanced Autonomous Parking Solutions with Transfer Learning for Smart Cities
pmc-10650556.creator: Qaiser Abbas, Gulzar Ahmad, Tahir Alyas, Turki Alghamdi, Yazed Alsaawy, Ali Alzahrani
pmc-10650556.description: Smart cities have emerged as a specialized domain encompassing various technologies, transitioning from civil engineering to technology-driven solutions. The accelerated development of technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), software-defined networks (SDN), 5G, artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and analytics, has played a crucial role in providing solutions for smart cities.

pmc-10723579.title: Voice and Communication Training Program Improves Performance of University Students in Oral Presentations
pmc-10723579.creator: Deborah Cristine Bonetti Rosa, Leonardo Wanderley Lopes, Simone Aparecida Lopes-Herrera, Deborah Cristine Bonetti Rosa, Leonardo Wanderley Lopes, Simone Aparecida Lopes-Herrera
pmc-10723579.description: PurposeTo investigate the effect of a voice and communication training program for oral presentations on higher education students.MethodsThe proposed training program was based on the areas of social skills, voice projection techniques, and neurolinguistic programming. Thirty-eight students participated in the training with active learning methodologies at the university.

pmc-10809992.title: An examination of the effects of family, school, and community resilience on high school students’ resilience in China
pmc-10809992.creator: Chunlin Qi, Nanchang Yang
pmc-10809992.description: IntroductionResilience plays a pivotal role in shaping the academic accomplishments, psychological well-being, and future prospects of high school students. Despite its significance, there is a notable dearth of studies examining the current state and determinants of resilience among high school students in China.

pmc-11353616.description: The purpose of this study was to substitute shortening with olive diacylglycerol oil/candelilla wax (OCW)–olive diacylglycerol stearin (ODS) oleogels and evaluate their impact on starch digestibility in cookies. The in vitro digestibility study confirmed that the OCW/ODS–based cookies exhibited a notable enhancement of 14.6% in slowly digestible starch (SDS) and an increase of 3.

pmc-11602590.title: Identifying compound-protein interactions with knowledge graph embedding of perturbation transcriptomics
pmc-11602590.creator: Shengkun Ni, Xiangtai Kong, Yingying Zhang, Zhengyang Chen, Zhaokun Wang, Zunyun Fu, Ruifeng Huo, Xiaochu Tong, Ning Qu, Xiaolong Wu, Kun Wang, Wei Zhang, Runze Zhang, Zimei Zhang, Jiangshan Shi, Yitian Wang, Ruirui Yang, Xutong Li, Sulin Zhang, Mingyue Zheng
pmc-11602590.description: SummaryThe emergence of perturbation transcriptomics provides a new perspective for drug discovery, but existing analysis methods suffer from inadequate performance and limited applicability. In this work, we present PertKGE, a method designed to deconvolute compound-protein interactions from perturbation transcriptomics with knowledge graph embedding.

pmc-11619136.title: The host genotype actively shapes its microbiome across generations in laboratory mice
pmc-11619136.creator: Laurentiu Benga, Anna Rehm, Christina Gougoula, Philipp Westhoff, Thorsten Wachtmeister, W Peter M Benten, Eva Engelhardt, Andreas P M Weber, Karl Köhrer, Martin Sager, Stefan Janssen
pmc-11619136.description: BackgroundThe microbiome greatly affects health and wellbeing. Evolutionarily, it is doubtful that a host would rely on chance alone to pass on microbial colonization to its offspring. However, the literature currently offers only limited evidence regarding two alternative hypotheses: active microbial shaping by host genetic factors or transmission of a microbial maternal legacy.

pmc-11692120.title: PARTNER CORRESPONDENCE IN SOCIAL INTERACTION TIME AND WELL-BEING: EVERYDAY EVIDENCE FROM OLDER DYADS
pmc-11692120.creator: Carlotta Grünjes, Elizabeth Zambrano Garza, Rachel Murphy, Kenneth Madden, Denis Gerstorf, Gizem Hueluer, Christiane Hoppmann
pmc-11692120.description: Social interactions play an important role in older adults’ daily well-being. Longer duration of interaction has been associated with higher well-being at the individual level. However, less is known about the extent to which partners differ in their convergence in interaction reports and whether such differences might be associated with daily well-being.

pmc-12548190.title: Multivariate screening of upland cotton genotypes reveals key traits for salt tolerance at the seedling stage
pmc-12548190.creator: Zunaira Anwar, Allah Ditta, Muhammad Kashif Riaz Khan
pmc-12548190.description: BackgroundSoil salinity poses a serious threat to cotton production worldwide by impairing growth, yield, and fiber quality. Salt stress disrupts key morphological, physiological, and biochemical processes in cotton plants, leading to considerable reductions in productivity. Therefore, identifying salt-tolerant cotton genotypes is essential for improving crop performance in saline environments.

pmc-13065614.title: Mine Waste Disasters on the Zambian Copperbelt: Regulatory and Community Concerns
pmc-13065614.creator: Charles Poleni Mukumba, Makweti Sishekanu, Lochner Marais
pmc-13065614.description: The accumulated waste produced by a mine can pose risks to communities in the vicinity. Three disasters occurring within 15 months on the Zambian Copperbelt have refocused attention on mine waste management and disasters in Africa. The paper investigates these three disasters in the light of the changing regulatory environment and liberalisation of the mining sector in Zambia.

pmc-13242224.title: Reassessment of Childhood Peanut Allergy Reveals Tolerance
pmc-13242224.creator: Shreena G Reddy, Vishaka R Hatcher, Charles K Miller
pmc-13242224.description: Peanut allergy is commonly diagnosed in childhood and may persist as a medical label into adulthood despite the development of clinical tolerance, leading to potential misclassification and unnecessary dietary and occupational restrictions. We report a 19-year-old male patient with a childhood diagnosis of peanut allergy that precluded military enlistment in the United States despite years of reported asymptomatic peanut ingestion.

pmc-13377551.title: Efficacy of Select Gene Targets for the Management of Western Flower Thrips Through RNA Interference
pmc-13377551.creator: C. M. Senthil Kumar, Ritesh G. Jain, Stephen J. Fletcher, Neena Mitter, Karl E. Robinson
pmc-13377551.description: Western flower thrips (WFT) Frankliniella occidentalis cause extensive damage to crops either by direct feeding injury or by transmitting diseases. Current management strategies against this pest rely heavily on synthetic insecticides, leading to issues such as resistance development and environmental concerns.

pmc-13435871.title: Iron status, hepcidin, and CRP in children with endoscopically confirmed adenotonsillar hypertrophy: a controlled cross-sectional study
pmc-13435871.creator: Serhan Keskin, Nurşen Keskin
pmc-13435871.description: BackgroundAdenotonsillar hypertrophy (ATH) may influence iron homeostasis through low-grade inflammation and upper airway obstruction, but findings in children remain inconsistent. This study aimed to compare hematologic, iron-related, and inflammatory parameters in school-aged children with and without endoscopically confirmed ATH.MethodsThis controlled cross-sectional study included 300 children aged 6–12 years (150 with ATH and 150 controls).

pmc-13493831.title: AdaptiveFrequencyNet: a long-term time series forecasting approach based on learnable frequency decomposition and cross-scale attention fusion
pmc-13493831.creator: JiaoJiao Cui, Wei Li, Xin Wang
pmc-13493831.description: Long-term time series forecasting depends on modeling variation across time scales together with persistent temporal dependence. Existing frequency decomposition methods partially address multi-scale modeling but suffer from fixed frequency decomposition, simplistic feature fusion, and insufficient cross-scale interaction. Fixed splits can also shift the predictive distribution away from the input scale, which hurts long-horizon consistency.

uslaw-usc-t25-s2720.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s2720.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 29 (Indian Gaming Regulation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Consistent with the requirements of this chapter, sections 1301, 1302, 1303 and 1304 of title 18 shall not apply to any gaming conducted by an Indian tribe pursuant to this chapter.

uslaw-usc-t34-s40102.description: United States Code, Title 34 (Crime Control And Law Enforcement); Chapter 401 (Child Abuse Crime Information And Background Checks). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general (1) A State may have in effect procedures (established by State statute or regulation) that require qualified entities designated by the State to contact an authorized agency of the State to request a nationwide background.
